2607.05790.title: Controlling Tool Use with Heading-Specific Activation Steering
2607.05790.paper_summary: Tool-augmented large language models extend their capabilities beyond parametric knowledge through external tools, but tend to invoke them unnecessarily. We investigate whether tool-use decisions have any stable internal representation that can be extracted and manipulated, a question that is non-trivial given that tools exist entirely in context at inference time and have no direct encoding in model weights. We show that steering vectors extracted from heading-anchors positions exert bidirectional causal control over tool-invocation behavior across five open-source models and three domains, suppressing unnecessary tool use most effectively in domains where parametric reasoning suffices. However, geometric analysis reveals that this causal effectiveness does not correspond to clean linear structure: tool-invocation steps exhibit diffuse, bimodal alignment with the suppression vector rather than the consistent negative alignment a linear encoding account would predict, and different tool types recruit largely distinct internal signatures with low cross-tool feature overlap. We hypothesize these geometric properties are indicative of the non-parametric nature of tools, and distinguish tool-use steering vectors from those extracted for parametrically grounded concepts. The relationship between this geometric irregularity and the observed causal effectiveness remains an open question.
2607.05790.paper_summary_zh: 工具增強的大型語言模型通過外部工具擴展其能力，超越了參數知識，但往往不必要地調用它們。<lb/>我們調查工具使用決策是否具有任何穩定的內部表示，可以被提取和操作，這是一個非平凡的問題，因為工具在推理時完全存在於上下文中，並且在模型權重中沒有直接的編碼。<lb/>我們展示了從標題錨點位置提取的引導向量對五個開源模型和三個領域的工具調用行為施加了雙向因果控制，在參數推理足夠的領域中最有效地抑制了不必要的工具使用。<lb/>然而，幾何分析顯示這種因果有效性並不對應於清晰的線性結構：工具調用步驟與抑制向量表現出擴散的雙峰對齊，而不是線性編碼模型所預測的一致負對齊，不同的工具類型招募了大致不同的內部特徵簽名，並且工具之間的特徵重疊較低。<lb/>我們假設這些幾何特性表明工具的非參數性質，並將工具使用引導向量與為參數基礎概念提取的向量區分開來。<lb/>這種幾何不規則性與觀察到的因果有效性之間的關係仍然是一個未解的問題。
